questions.q: Why give each project its own virtual environment?
options: Each project gets its own installed packages and versions, so two projects can need different versions without fighting
It's required to run any Python
questions.explain: In the lab, project-a's venv has requests 2.34.2 and project-b's has 2.33.1, side by side.

options: A folder with its own python, its own pip, and its own empty place for packages
questions.explain: .venv/bin/pip installs into that folder only; nothing else is touched.

questions.q: Why write requests==2.34.2 (and pin its dependencies) instead of just requests?
options: pip can't install without a version
So every computer installs exactly the same versions, today and next month
questions.explain: In the lab, removing certifi's pin made pip install a 2-day-old version. Exact pins make installs repeatable.

options: Makes plain python and pip in this shell mean the venv's own (by putting .venv/bin first in PATH)
questions.explain: which python then shows /lab/project-a/.venv/bin/python. deactivate undoes it.

questions.q: Should you commit the .venv folder to Git?
options: No: it's big and machine-specific; commit requirements.txt (or pyproject.toml + a lock file) and rebuild the venv from it
questions.explain: The lab's .gitignore lists .venv/. Anyone can recreate it with one command.

questions.q: pyproject.toml says bazaar = "bazaar.main:start", but main.py only has run(). What happens when you type bazaar list?
questions.explain: pip writes a script that imports exactly the function named in [project.scripts]. Fix the name and reinstall.

questions.q: (Going deeper) What is a lock file like uv.lock?
options: A file that stops others from editing code
A generated list of the exact version (and hash) of every package, including dependencies
questions.explain: You list the few packages you want; the tool works out and records everything else, so installs are repeatable.

questions.q: (Going deeper) Why does this course only pin versions released at least two weeks ago?
options: Brand-new releases occasionally have bugs or are even malicious; waiting a little lets problems get found first
questions.explain: Installing a package runs other people's code. Pinning, waiting a little, and checking for typo-named lookalikes are basic supply-chain safety.
